findings.evidence: “This skill is a Process ... executed with Tool-level rigor” labels the rubric pattern without teaching the agent a decision. The adjacent factory-subcommand rule and its reason do add repository-specific knowledge.
findings.fix: Keep the fixed step order and the reason to use the factory subcommands. Record removal of the rubric labels, which do not guide the wizard.

findings.evidence: The Step 2 table says “I want to... | Go to,” presenting vendor resolution, pair storage and testing as independent destinations even though the wizard calls them in a specific order.
findings.fix: Turn the table into a phase map: Step 2.1 gates target and replacement; Step 2.2 drives the question order; Steps 2.3–2.8 are helpers called by that flow, not alternate entry points. Keep the links to each helper.

findings.evidence: The description says “Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup,” but does not cue stale-provider checks or distinguish setup from running existing lanes or editing unrelated config. “Force local write without asking” also obscures the separate replacement gate.
findings.fix: Use when someone wants to set up or refresh ai-kit’s cross-AI review or execute lanes, pick models for a second opinion or coding fallback, check reviewer availability or stale OpenCode providers, or ask what happens to an old review-spec.toml. Detect installed CLIs, propose separate review and execute sets from the model catalog, and record the owner’s picks, order, effort and opt-ins in [lanes]. Default to the project’s .aikit/config.toml; --local and --global select the target but never authorize replacement. Announce the exact path and ask before replacing an existing roster. --check-only reports without writing config, persistent caches or trust. Also use when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup because lanes are missing. Not for running existing lanes, editing [runner], or adding provider credentials.

findings.evidence: The 492-line, roughly 7,300-word body loads the full “When the write target was local” trust procedure even for global writes, ordinary runtime pairs and availability-only runs. Most of the detail is needed only when a local command-bearing entry requires trust.
findings.fix: Keep the command-bearing test and explicit-consent stop in Step 4. Move the detailed preview, migration, cross-role and revoke branches into a focused references/trust-local.md, linked directly from Step 4 only when a local entry needs trust or a normal probe reports an untrusted local roster. Preserve all fail-closed checks in that destination.

findings.evidence: “Loaded from wizard-flow.md step 2 only” conflicts with the explicit Step 6 route to item 6. A kept lane with complete catalog data can need item 6 without needing the discovery instructions.
findings.fix: List both entry points at the top: Step 2 reads items 1–4 for missing listings or unmatched candidates; Step 6 reads item 6 for the code-index check and skips the catalog-refresh instructions.

findings.evidence: “--global forces <user config> directly” and “--local also forces local directly,” but there is no rule for both flags together. The agent is left to choose a write scope, even though the wider scope affects other projects.
findings.fix: Treat --local and --global as mutually exclusive. If both are supplied, stop before discovery or writes and ask the owner to choose exactly one. Keep the separate replacement gate for the chosen scope.

findings.evidence: The router-alias assertion begins “If the proposal shows an alias group,” so a run can pass after omitting the group. The supplied fixture only contains lane text and does not guarantee that the catalog or proposal emits an alias row.
findings.fix: Supply a deterministic catalog or proposal fixture with one owner-defined alias and require that the output show that alias, the exact assumption label, no rank or score, and no heuristic confirmation question.

findings.evidence: The set has 10 positives and 10 negatives, including useful near-misses, but negatives such as “Write a unit test for the parser in the markdown-to-pdf skill” test little about where lane setup ends.
findings.fix: Replace clearly unrelated negatives with realistic near-misses: diagnose quota exhaustion during an already configured review, change the host CLI’s default model without touching ai-kit, or install a missing reviewer CLI without registering a lane.

findings.evidence: “That call prints the same JSON lines ... when any differs ... --revoke” fails on an unchanged config. In skills/ai-kit-spec-review/ai_kit_spec/cli.py:1186–1198, --show adds trusted and path to argv records; the trusting form omits them. Literal comparison revokes valid consent and repeats the question.
findings.fix: Compare parsed records on their shared fields: key and argv, or key and error. Do not compare preview-only metadata or the final status line as argv rows. For command-bearing entries shown manually because the preview omitted them, require evidence that the approved roster and inherited command are unchanged; if that cannot be established, leave the file untrusted.

findings.evidence: Step 2.3 resolves “vendor” for each model, but Step 3’s “Each object in lanes carries” schema omits it, and the referenced JSON example omits it too. quota.py:48–50 and 87–93 read the stored vendor directly and do not infer it at selection, so a same-vendor lane with no vendor field can bypass the secondary reviewer’s vendor filter.
findings.fix: Carry the Step 2.3 vendor into the JSON for each named model, including a user-supplied vendor when inference returned null. Update the writer example and its round-trip assertion. Keep the session-default case distinct and do not invent its vendor.

findings.evidence: “detect-runtimes --save <runtimes.json>” refreshes the snapshot after SKILL.md Step 1.5 checks it for listing-less runtimes. If a listing fails on the refresh, fetch-model-catalog can call the migrating cfg_resolve on a roster the owner did not approve. The reference also gives no instruction to skip its fetch when Step 1.5 has already forbidden it.
findings.fix: Reuse Step 1’s saved snapshot by default. If discovery refreshes or extends it, repeat the pending-roster gate against the exact snapshot the fetch will consume. Put the no-fetch branch before the fetch in catalog.md and propagate it to all retries and candidate-refresh paths.

findings.evidence: “Any runtime but claude and copilot” does not exclude a custom command. The effort-probe example uses --runtime, but Step 2.4 says custom commands have no runtime field, and lane_effort.py:52–56 rejects a top-level effort on such a lane. A custom CLI can therefore be sent through the wrong test path and end up dropped by the writer.
findings.fix: Branch on lane type before asking about effort. Use the runner effort probe only for supported table runtimes. For a custom lane, use only its own template fields, pass those fields in --extra-json on the consented --command test, and never store the runner’s effort or effort_source keys.
